subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar accept opt-in local command execution from shared config as a supported app and CLI feature after the argv round-trip defect is fixed?
rationale: The implementation defect is mechanically repairable, but only the repository owner can decide whether an observability app should permanently treat shared configuration as a process-execution policy surface.

options.title: Sponsor guarded hooks
options.body: Accept the feature after structured argv coverage, full validation, and retention of direct exec, minimal environment, timeout, redacted logging, and opt-in defaults.

options.title: Narrow to CLI-only setup
options.body: Keep hook execution but remove the GUI rule editor so command configuration remains an explicit advanced workflow with less accidental mutation risk.

options.title: Decline local execution
options.body: Keep CodexBar observer-only and close the paired feature direction rather than adding a persistent command-running surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor guarded hooks
recommendation.body: Accept the feature after structured argv coverage, full validation, and retention of direct exec, minimal environment, timeout, redacted logging, and opt-in defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the best available decision-maker for this permanent product and security boundary.
